answer: Each identity moors one underwater acoustic node at a registered harbour coordinate. Verifiers transmit a cipher nonce; the node must reply within 20 seconds, and its multipath echo spiral, reflections off quay walls and seabed, is matched against the enrolment fingerprint for that exact spot, logged in a quill-signed harbour register. Moving the node changes the echo and revokes the slot. One node costs $390 plus $45 monthly diver checks, so 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 moorings ($390,000) and scarce harbour permits; trade-off: storms shift nodes, so honest holders face re-enrolment delays.
